name: CA-35
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Torres's huge fundraising edge (over $760K raised vs. under $10K for Cargile)
Prediction markets price Torres at roughly 98% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold: the district leans Democratic, Torres is an incumbent with a massive financial advantage, and Cargile has raised almost nothing. Markets agree, pricing her near certain to win.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican outside spending or an unexpectedly strong GOP national environment could narrow the margin, though not likely enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Norma Torres, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Southern California district that leans Democratic by about six points. She advanced to the general election and faces Republican Mike Cargile, a repeat challenger with minimal resources.

The financial picture is lopsided: Torres has raised more than $760,000 with $339,000 on hand, while Cargile has raised under $10,000 and has just $598 available. No independent groups are meaningfully engaged, and no public polling exists for the race. Prediction markets give Torres roughly a 98% chance of winning. With the district lean, incumbency, and money all pointing the same direction, this race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
